title: Explorer
build: a freezer backup of Electric Dreams' 1987 disk release, the TOSEC image Explorer (1987)(Electric Dreams) from the Internet Archive (MD5 858dc180…672db); its code agrees byte for byte with Triad's crack of the same release

records.c: the high byte of the screen the game draws into: $40 (bank 1, bitmap $6000) or $C0 (bank 3, bitmap $E000); swap_buffers flips it, and the other value is the screen on show
second operand of the 16-bit arithmetic routines (with $0B)
operand of the 16-bit arithmetic routines (with $0D), and the pointer to a string or an image for the drawing routines
the 16-bit accumulator of the arithmetic routines (with $0F), and the column and row for the drawing routines
pointer used for tables and records (with $11)
the explorer's east-west position, 16 bits (with $1A); the view from above keeps it on a multiple of 16
the explorer's north-south position, 16 bits (with $1C)
the point the terrain routines are asked about, 16 bits (with $21)
with $23, the probe's north-south coordinate
the height terrain_at returns for the probe (with $25); $C8 for water
the kind of ground terrain_at returns: 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 by the heights of the layers, $0A for water
the low byte of the last layer's sum, kept by scenery_list_for; 12 makes the cell a doorway (scenery_doorway)
0 while the far ring of scenery is drawn, 2 for the near ring
one layer's height sum (with $2A), from layer_sum_at

the first of the two random bytes rnd_next steps (with rnd_b at $2C); seeded from the raster line at start, and again from the ground's height (ground_height) at the start of every cell's scenery in draw_scenery_at, so the objects at a place come out the same at every visit
the column, 0-63 round the horizon, where the next scenery object is drawn
pointer to the list of objects still to draw at one scenery position (with $2F)
the object draw_object draws: its number, negative for the mirror image
the explorer's position rounded down to the 16-unit grid (with $34), set by draw_ground_view
with $36, the north-south half of the grid cell
the compass bearing on the ground, 0-63 (64 steps to the circle, 16 to a right angle)
how many key codes wait in key_buffer
fragments found, shown as the score; each one counts once
16 bits (with $44); 40,000 at the start, 2,000 after it runs out
the attribute print_string gives each letter; $C0 leaves the colour as it is
the result of bearing_of, in degrees (with $69)
1 while a bug is on the view
up to ten key codes, oldest first
when not zero, the attribute every drawing routine uses instead of the image's own; the map's beacon cells use $C0 here
1 from zp_image, and nothing writes it: scan_keys repeats held keys
the length of the name typed at a doorway
the name typed at a doorway, up to 32 characters
what swap_buffers sets the video chip to: 1 extended-colour text (the view from above), 2 hires bitmap (the ground)
1 while the ground view is drawn for a landing, so no bug appears in it
the time left on tone_wait's tone (with $9F), counted down by the interrupt

the two bytes before the game's entry: $0800 is the zero BASIC needs before a program, and $0801-$0802 hold the start of the backup's BASIC line, which Triad's crack has as other values; the game never reads them

the game's entry, where the release's loader jumps: sets up the machine (init_machine), shows the title until a key or fire (wait_key), zooms the planet in (zoom_in) and picks the start position at random from the raster line; then flies the opening pass over the map with the map loop's key reading switched off (the RTS stored at $2847), puts fragment 1 at 160 east and 144 north of the start position (the pass scrolls only the map's edges, not the position), and lands at the centre of the map the pass ended on (go_down at height 8), which on jungle or water is a crash

the opening fly-over: 80 steps, each scrolling the map one cell north (scroll_north); at step 40 the screen shakes (shake), and a key pressed meanwhile (key_get) also scrolls it one cell east when its code is even (8, for one) or west when it is odd (5)
restores the JSR at $2847, so the map loop reads keys again

shakes the screen ten times: the fine-scroll bits of $D016 set to 7 and those of $D011 to 0, then $D016's back to 0 and $D011's back to their usual 7, with delay_short between, and the map scrolled north at each pass

swaps attribute bytes on the screen on show, all four pages: each byte equal to tmp2 becomes tmp3 and the reverse, and each equal to tmp4 becomes tmp5 and the reverse; then waits three times delay_short. hud_twinkle calls it with $9C/$C9 and $72/$27
a delay loop of 14 x 256 passes, about 18,000 cycles
sets the horizontal fine scroll ($D016 bits 0-2) to 0
sets the horizontal fine scroll to 7
sets the vertical fine scroll ($D011 bits 0-2) to 0
sets the vertical fine scroll to 7

plays a tone on voice 3 and waits for it to end: frequency from we, length in interrupts from wc, which the interrupt counts down in tone_time; the sonar's pings and their echoes. Silences the SID first (sid_reset)
the interrupt's countdown of tone_time, by one each interrupt, until it reaches zero

waits for a key and returns its code in A; while there is none it saves zero page $09-$13, lets the head-up display twinkle (hud_twinkle) and a bug move (bug_move), and puts them back. Clicks (key_click) when a key comes
copies zero page $09-$13 to saved_work
copies saved_work back to zero page $09-$13
eleven bytes where save_work keeps zero page $09-$13 while wait_key runs other routines
the RTS bug_move's early exits share

moves the bug one step while the game waits for a key, if one is out (bug_active): the low four bits of the raster line pick the step (bit 0 right, bit 1 left, bit 2 up, bit 3 down; the values 0, 3, 12 and 15 make it stay); it restores the background under the old position from the screen on show (restore_cell, six cells), redraws the bug (bug_image) at the new one and the gun sight over it, and swaps the screens

the start-up: copies zero page's first values from zp_image, clears colour RAM, copies the character set to the second bank, sets CIA 2 for VIC bank 3, sets the screen and charset pointers, turns the bitmap on, sets the background colours for extended-colour text (5, 7, 3 and 2), blacks the border, points the interrupt at irq and the NMI at an RTI, and enables interrupts
silences the SID: clears its 24 registers and sets the volume to 15
the interrupt, from CIA 1's timer: counts the tone down (tone_tick), scans the keyboard and joystick (scan_keys), acknowledges CIA 1 and returns
the RTI the NMI vector points at, so RESTORE does nothing

reads the keyboard matrix and joystick port 2 once an interrupt: finds the key held down (keymap gives its code, keymap_shifted when a shift key is held), and with no key the joystick (joy_codes). A new key goes into key_buffer at once; a key held down is added again after 16 interrupts and then every fourth interrupt, each time only if the buffer is empty. The branch for key_repeat_on clear, which would add a held key every interrupt, never runs: nothing changes it from 1
no key is down: reads joystick port 2 through $DC00 and turns its direction and fire bits into a key code (joy_codes)

32 key codes indexed by the joystick's five bits, read active-high: up gives '7' (forward, north), down '6' (about turn, south), left '5', right '8', fire 'F'; diagonals take up or down, up and down together give '7', the other combinations without fire give 'B', and every combination with fire gives 'F'
the key code for each of the 64 keyboard matrix positions, scanned from column 0 ($DC00 = $FE) row by row, upper case; 1 marks a shift key, $3F a key with no code, $FF the end
the same 65 entries with a shift key held: lower-case letters and the shifted punctuation
copies zp_image to zero page, all 256 bytes ($00 and $01 included, which set the processor port to $2F/$05: RAM with the I/O area)

the 256 bytes zp_init copies to zero page at start; the first 160 set the game's variables: energy 40,000 ($43), key repeat on ($78), the drawing page $40, empty fix and nearest results; the last 96 are the bytes after the table (the doorway code at $0D32 and its strings), which land in zero page $A0-$FF unused
the explorer has walked into a doorway: draws a window, "Enter doorway" and "(other keys skip)", and waits for a key: E goes through (enter_doorway), any other key redraws the view
"Enter doorway", zero-terminated
"(other keys skip)"
"Name the spot you wish to go to:" and eight spaces

the test for the end of the game: if all nine fragments' positions (fragments) equal the explorer's grid cell, draws a window with "WOW, YOU DID IT!" and stops there for good; otherwise returns at the first that differs
the game's end: a jump to itself, with the win message on the screen
"WOW, YOU DID IT!"
the RTS check_win returns by when a fragment is elsewhere

the doorway's trip, also where a crash or running out of energy sends the explorer: draws the destination prompt (str_name_spot), reads a name (read_name), and turns it into a position. East: from 0, for each letter in order, add the letter, then rotate the 16 bits and the carry of that sum left five times; north: the same, over name_buf backwards from the zero after the name down to its second letter. HOME goes to 48,356 east and 48,609 north, in every game. Then works out an energy change (the name's length less 8, times 512, less a quarter of the distance gone, east plus north) but jumps past the store either way, so the trip costs nothing; then draws the ground there
unreached: the store of the doorway's energy change into energy (lda we, sta energy, lda we_hi, sta energy_hi), which both branches before it jump over
the other branch of the doorway's energy test, to the same place as the first
fills the screen on show (draw_page EOR $80), 480 two-byte steps from $00, with the pair $27, $72, so that its colours come out in stripes
reads a name into name_buf: up to 32 characters, letters folded to upper case, DEL rubs one out, RETURN ends; each character is drawn at input_col, input_row as it is typed
prints name_buf at the input position (print_string)

prints the compass bearing on the ground view at column 36, row 1, as three digits: v = (320 - 4 x heading) mod 256 is the heading clockwise from north in 256ths of a circle; t = 7v/8, and the degrees are t + t/2 + t/16 + t/32, each part rounded down. That is about 1.395 v where a circle needs 1.406 v: 0 for north, 88 for east, 178 for south, 267 for west, 349 one step west of north
saves the three colour cells at screen offset $4C and the 24 bitmap bytes behind them, from the screen on show, into compass_cells
puts back what save_compass_cells saved, into the screen on show
three colour cells and 24 bitmap bytes kept by save_compass_cells
compass_cells's 24 bitmap bytes, after its three colour bytes
divides the byte in we by the byte in wb, we_hi zero on entry, by eight steps of shift and subtract: the quotient goes into we and the remainder into we_hi; wb_hi counts the steps

draws the scenery of one grid cell around the explorer, at horizon column A + 4: finds the ground at the probe (terrain_at), takes the scenery list for its kind (scenery_list_for), seeds the random bytes with the ground's height, and draws a chain of objects: a list's first byte counts its entries, and the entry used is a random byte mixed with the random bytes' new values, modulo the count (divide_8), plus one, or the first once three objects are drawn; each object drawn names the list its successor comes from (draw_object), and an entry of 0 ends the chain. The same place therefore always shows the same objects. Then the doorway, when the cell's last layer sum ends in the byte 12, and a beacon, when one has been dropped within 8 units of the probe
after the objects: a cell whose last layer sum has the low byte 12 is a doorway, drawn in front of the explorer (draw_doorway)
a dropped beacon within 8 units of the probe is drawn in front of the explorer (draw_beacon)
draws the doorway, the flashing striped patch doorway_image, at column 17, row 20, with its own attribute ($F2, flashing red on yellow) forced on every cell
draws beacon_image at column 24, row 20, with its own attributes forced
draws fragment number tmp9: its image from fragment_images, at column 5 and row 22 moved by its pair in fragment_offsets, so that the fragments in one cell pile up at the bottom left
the address of each of the nine fragments' pictures, 2 x 2 cells each, from $B728 to $B868 in steps of 40 bytes
fragment_images's high bytes, read one byte on
a column and a row offset for each fragment's place in the pile: (0,-6), (2,-5), (0,-4), (2,-3), (0,-2), (2,-1), (0,0), (2,0), (1,-7)
fragment_offsets's rows, read one byte on
draws every fragment whose position (fragments) is the explorer's grid cell, with a short sound (sfx_fragment) for each

draws the view on the ground into the hidden screen: takes 15 from energy (energy_spend); rounds the position to the grid (cell_x, cell_y); clears the bitmap; colours 17 rows of sky and 4 of ground; draws the distant hills (hill_columns); draws the scenery of the 16 cells two cells away and then of the 8 cells one away, each at its compass column relative to the heading (draw_scenery_at), with three rows of near ground between; then the explorer's own cell: a beacon, a fragment (the first sight of each adds one to the score and its digit to the Found list), the fragments lying there, and, unless landing or a bug is out, a new bug at random, more likely as the score rises
the far ring is drawn with scene_near 0, the near one with 2

the distant hills, 64 columns round the horizon of which the 40 facing the heading show: the height of hill i is entry 4i of terrain_profile divided by 32, drawn as a stack of that many cells under a crest (hill_images) ending at row 17. The skyline is the same everywhere on the planet and turns only with the heading
the far ring: from two cells north, round the square of cells two away, 16 cells, each four columns further round the horizon
three rows of near ground (attribute $60, bright green) at rows 21-23, then the near ring, the 8 cells next to the explorer's, eight columns apart
the explorer's own cell: a beacon there, and the fragments

a fragment within 8 units of the cell (fragment_at_probe, which numbers them 1-9): the first time, its digit goes into the Found list, one place after the colon for fragment 1, and the score goes up by one

a new bug, only if none is out and the view is not a landing: one appears when the raster line's low byte is below score + 1, so more often as the score rises; its picture is one of bug_images (a random byte divided by 5, the remainder), its place in columns 3-34 and rows 4-19 from the raster line, and the weapons mode starts at once (weapons)
the addresses of the five bug pictures, $4980 to $4A70 in steps of 60 bytes
the picture of the bug that is out (with $14C3)
bug_image's high byte
the bug's column on the screen
the bug's row
the picture of the gun's sight, sight_picture at $4AAC (with $14C7)
sight_image's high byte
the sight's column, 12 at the start
the sight's row, 19 at the start
moves the probe 16 units east (probe_x up), and returns the heading in A with the carry clear for the caller to add a column to
moves the probe 16 units west
moves the probe 16 units north
moves the probe 16 units south
the ground's main loop: draws and shows the view, then waits for a key: 8 turns right, 5 left (two steps of 64 each), 6 turns about, 7 walks, U takes off; every other key opens the menu
walking: steps forward (step_forward) until a key comes or a step is blocked (step_forward then bumps and goes back to ground_loop); 8 and 5 turn while walking, 7 steps again, any other key stops
the step stands: the end-of-game and doorway tests, and the view at the new position (after_step), then the walking zoom (walk_zoom)
turning while walking: redraws the view and walks on
8 while walking: turns right two steps
5 while walking: turns left two steps
8 standing: turns right two steps
5 standing: turns left two steps
6: turns about, 32 steps
17 values of 16 x sine for the angles 0 to 90 degrees in steps of 5.625 (0, 2, 3, 5, ... 16): the step forward for each heading
the step of 16 units for heading A (0-63, counter-clockwise from east): returns the east step in wc and the north step in wc_hi, signed, from sine_table by quadrant

one step of 16 units along the heading (heading_step). Before it stands, the attribute of the cell at row 3, column 19 of the view on show is compared with $30 (black on yellow): if they match, something stands in the way, so the old position is kept, a bump sounds (sfx_bump) and the view is redrawn; otherwise the step stands (after_step)

after a step: checks for the end of the game (check_win), then whether the cell at row 19, column 19 of the view on show has the doorway's attribute ($F2); if so asks about the doorway (doorway_prompt), otherwise draws the view at the new position
redraws the view and returns
E at the doorway: a sound (sfx_doorway), two fades, then drops the return address and goes to the destination prompt (name_destination)

unreached: 66 bytes of code no instruction calls or jumps to, which would copy the view's colours between the two screens (from $4000 to $C028 and $40E6 to $C10E, or the other way when draw_page is $C0)

U on the ground: puts the compass cells back, a rising sound, and 18 steps of the view sliding down one row with a row of sky added at the top (scroll_down), the pitch going up three each step; takes 100 from energy and goes up to the view from above (fly)
"Impossible"
"Not dropped"
"Out of range"
"Objects", the menu's first line
"Beacons"
"Weapons"
"Energy", with six spaces that menu fills with the energy left
the six places menu fills with the energy left
"Score", with three spaces for the score
the three places menu fills with the score
"Echo nearest", the objects menu
"Send to beacon"
"Found:" and nine spaces, where the digits of the fragments seen go
the Found list's place in str_found: fragment n's digit goes n places after the colon here
"Drop beacon", the beacons menu
"Pick up beacon"
"Fix 3 nearest"
"Carried:012345678", the digits of the beacons carried, each replaced by a space when it is dropped
"<arrows>", the weapons mode's first line
"Fire"
"graphics: Simon Dunstan", shown by X in the menu
" program: Graham Relf"
the row tables are read from one byte before their start by the map's tile drawing (draw_map_tile), which adds 1 to the row
the low byte of each text row's offset in a screen, row x 40, rows 0-24 (with row_offset_hi)
the low bytes of rows 20-24, the last of row_offset_lo
row_offset_hi read one byte before, by draw_map_tile
the high byte of each text row's offset
the high bytes of rows 20-24, the last of row_offset_hi

the head-up display's menu (any key on the ground but the moves): a window with Objects, Beacons, Weapons, the energy left and the score; then O opens the objects menu, B the beacons menu, W the weapons, X the credits, any other key closes it
the objects menu: Echo nearest, Send to beacon, and the Found list; E echoes, S sends, any other key closes

the sonar: a ping (tone_wait), then finds the nearest fragment (nearest_fragment); if it is within 1,279 units (the high byte of its distance below 5) a low tone lasts a quarter of the distance in interrupts and the echo sounds after it. Then its bearing in degrees in a window, and "Out of range" under it when there was no echo
"To which beacon?"
the number of the fragment send_to_beacon is sending

sends the fragment lying in the explorer's cell to a beacon, the anti-grav drone: "Impossible" when none lies there; asks "To which beacon?" and takes a digit 0-8; "Impossible" for any other key, "Not dropped" for a beacon still carried, "Out of range" when the beacon is 16,384 units or more away (the sum of the distances east and north); otherwise the fragment's position becomes the beacon's, 1,000 is taken from energy, and the view is redrawn with a sound (sfx_drone)
the beacons menu: Drop beacon, Pick up beacon, Fix 3 nearest, and the Carried list; D, P and F choose
drops the lowest-numbered beacon still carried at the explorer's grid cell (place_beacon); "Impossible" when all nine are down
picks up a dropped beacon within 32 units each way (take_beacon); "Impossible" when there is none
the line fix_beacons prints for each beacon: its digit, its distance, "m.", its bearing and "degrees"

Fix 3 nearest: finds the three nearest dropped beacons (find_three_beacons) and prints a line for each, the nearest on the last line: its number, its distance in metres (the sum of the distances east and north) and its bearing in degrees (bearing_of, wrong in the south-west quarter)
prints fix_line at the row in we_hi, column 2
writes the number in we as six characters (number_to_text) into the string at wc
waits for a key, then closes the window
wipes the window (restore_view)
a window with "Impossible", then a key closes it
prints the message at wc in the window's first line, waits for a key and closes it
a window with "Not dropped"
"Out of range" on the window's second line
X in the menu: a window with "program: Graham Relf" and "graphics: Simon Dunstan"
rewrites the digits of the Carried list: each beacon's digit if it is carried, a space if it is down; then redraws the view and sounds sfx_drop
six characters number_to_text writes a number into, right-aligned; the last three also serve as the score's and the key's place
number_text's last three characters, where menu takes the score from
the digit typed for send_to_beacon, printed after the question
writes the 16-bit number in we as decimal into number_text, right-aligned in spaces: takes digits off by divide_10, then a second pass carries any digit that came out as 10

divides we by ten by multiplying it by a binary fraction near one tenth: the quotient in we, the remainder in A and tmp9. For one value in ten the quotient comes out one too low and the remainder 10 more (6,553 of the 65,536 values), which number_to_text corrects
shows the hidden screen (swap_buffers), keeps what lies under the compass (save_compass_cells) and prints the compass (draw_compass)
drops beacon A, if it is carried: writes the explorer's grid cell as its position and the bytes in wb ($10, $27) after it, which mark it down; returns A 0, or 1 when the beacon was down already
picks up the first dropped beacon within 32 units of the grid cell each way: its last byte becomes $FF (carried); returns A 0, or 1 when there is none
finds a fragment within 8 units of the probe each way: returns its number counted from 1 (1-9) with Z set, or Y = 1 and Z clear when there is none
finds a dropped beacon within 8 units of the probe each way: returns its number with Z set, or Z clear when there is none
the distance east-west from the probe to the record at ptr, less 8: carry set when it is under 8
the same north-south

finds the three nearest dropped beacons to the grid cell: three passes over the nine, each taking the nearest (by the sum of the distances east and north) not already taken, with its distance, number and bearing (bearing_to); fix_dist, fix_bearing and fix_index hold the result of each pass, moved up five bytes after it
finds the fragment nearest the grid cell, by the sum of the distances east and north: its distance in near_dist, its number in near_index and its bearing in degrees (bearing_to) in near_bearing
the bearing in degrees from the grid cell to the record at ptr (bearing_of)
the nine beacons, six bytes each: east and north position (16 bits each), then two bytes: $FF $FF while it is carried, $10 $27 once it is dropped; all nine are carried at the start

the nine fragments of the spacecraft, four bytes each: east and north position, 16 bits each, in the order the game numbers them 1 to 9. Fragment 1's is set 160 east and 144 north of the start; the other eight are fixed, the same in every game
fragment 1's east position, high byte (set at the start)
fragment 1's north position, low byte
fragment 1's north position, high byte, then fragments 2-9 at $2217-$2236
copies 30 pages of bitmap between the screens with the copy loop at $227C, its addresses set from draw_page
copies the screen on show's colours (960 bytes) into the hidden screen with the same loop
the copy loop: its load and store addresses (copy_from, copy_to) are written by its callers
the address the copy loop reads (the operand of the LDA at $227C)
copy_from's high byte
the address the copy loop writes (the operand of the STA at $227F)
copy_to's high byte, which copy_bitmap and copy_screen set
copies the screen on show, bitmap and colours, into the hidden one, so the next window is drawn over the same view
copies the hidden screen, which holds the view without the window, over the screen on show (copy_shown_to_hidden with the pages swapped round), wiping the window drawn there
points ptr at beacon A's record (beacons + 6 x A)
points ptr at the record of the fragment the game numbers A + 1 (fragments + 4 x A)

opens a window at the top left of the view on show: attribute A, X cells wide and Y high inside; wipes any window there, draws a frame one cell wide round it (draw_frame) and fills the inside (fill_window); text in it is printed with its colour kept ($C0)

takes wc from energy; if the energy would go below zero it drops two return addresses, says "Energy gone", sets the energy to 2,000 and sends the explorer to the doorway's destination prompt (name_destination)
"Energy gone"
the energy has run out: drops energy_spend's caller and its caller, says "Energy gone", waits for a key and starts again at the destination prompt (name_destination) with 2,000
W in the menu: the weapons mode (weapons), then the view again

the weapons mode, which a bug starts and W in the menu opens: a window with "<arrows>" and "Fire"; the sight is drawn on the view and moved by 5, 8, 7 and 6 (left, right, up, down, kept inside columns 2-37 and rows 2-21), F fires (fire_laser); any other key leaves, but not while a bug is out
the bug is gone (or there was none): clears bug_active, redraws the view and empties the key buffer
5: the sight one column left, after putting back the cell under it (restore_cell)
8: the sight one column right
6: the sight one row down
7: the sight one row up

fires: the screen flashes red (flash_screen), a red square of 5 x 5 cells and then a square of 3 x 3 in a random colour are drawn round the sight, with the laser's sound; 500 is taken from energy. With no bug out the mode ends; a bug is hit when the sight's column is the bug's or one right of it and its row is the bug's or up to two above, and then it is gone; a miss puts the view back, redraws the bug and goes on aiming. The bug itself takes no energy: it holds the explorer in this mode until it is hit, and each shot costs 500
bug_move's step one column right (bug_step)
one column left
one row up
one row down

moves the bug by wc (columns) and wc_hi (rows) from the place in we, if the new place is inside columns 0-35 and rows 3-22: then it goes into bug_col, bug_row, with the old place in wc; otherwise we keeps the old place
copies one cell, its colour and its eight bitmap bytes, at column we, row we_hi from the hidden screen to the one on show: wipes what was drawn there on the screen on show
fills the colours of the screen on show with $2A (red on light red), 961 bytes
a delay of X x 256 passes of a loop of additions
the crash's sound: noise on voice 1 through the filter
a beacon dropped or picked up: a sawtooth on voice 1 warbling up and down 20 times
a safe landing's sound: voices 1 and 3 ring-modulated
a fragment sent to a beacon: voices 1 and 3 ring-modulated, higher
the sound as the view from above comes up
the laser: voice 1 ring-modulated by voice 3, both stepped to the raster line 200 times
unreached: 68 bytes of code no instruction calls or jumps to, a sound like sfx_drop that warbles from a higher pitch downwards
going through a doorway: a pulse wave on voice 2 whose width falls in 16 steps
the click of a key taken: a short triangle note on voice 2
a step blocked: a short noise on voice 1
a fragment in view: ring-modulated voices 1 and 3
taking off: voice 1 ring-modulated by voice 3, whose pitch take_off then raises

the height of the view from above: 8 when taking off, 9 after U; D at 9 comes down to 8, D at 8 lands

for each kind of ground (0, 2, 4, 6, 8 and water) and bits 1-2 of the last layer's sum (layer_sum, as terrain_at leaves it), the first of four characters in map_tile_chars: jungle for kinds 0 and 2, open ground for 4, open ground with a feature for some cells of 6 and 8, and water
sets the view from above to its start: 20 x 12 cells, 16 units apart, height 8

the view from above: extended-colour text, the map round the position, the flying sound; then its loop: 8 east, 7 north, 6 south and 5 west scroll the map one cell, U goes up, D goes down or lands. The attribute says how to draw: $28 leaves the colour as it is, $7F skips the cell, $80-$BF and $C0-$FF draw the pixels over the ground behind a mask (mask_keep_right, mask_keep_left), and the rest set the colour (attr_to_colour) and replace the eight bytes. attr_override and attr_force change this

a masked cell: the colour unless the attribute's low six bits are $28, then each byte ORed in after a mask has cleared the ground behind it (mask_keep_right for attributes $C0 and up, mask_keep_left for $80-$BF)

the bearing in degrees, clockwise from north, of a difference east (dx) and north (dy), 16 bits each: the smaller over the larger is found in tangent_table by a binary search of five halving steps from the middle (mul_8x16 for each try), giving an angle of 0-45 from the table's second half; when dx is the larger it becomes 90 less the angle. In the north-east quadrant that is the bearing; in the others quadrant_offsets gives 180, 360 or 270 less the angle. 270 less it is wrong for the south-west, where 180 plus it was needed: every bearing there comes out reflected about 225 degrees (264 reads 185, 186 reads 265). The result goes into bearing; zero page $0A-$11 are saved and restored
